input: The driver initially ticks no blackouts and explains that he sometimes misses radio messages because of reduced hearing, but later describes a delivery during which his colleague waved in front of him for several seconds before he responded; he remembers hearing the engine and seeing the loading bay, although he cannot recall the spoken exchange.
The colleague believes he was briefly unaware, while the driver thinks his hearing aid battery had failed, and neither account establishes whether consciousness was lost.

He has a history of noise exposure and uses one hearing aid inconsistently; a screening sheet lists left-ear thresholds of 45 dB at 500 Hz and 50 dB at 1000 Hz, but provides no right-ear values or results at 2000 and 3000 Hz.
He reports no hearing loss in quiet conversation, yet repeatedly asks the nurse to repeat questions when a fan is running, and there is no signed audiologist assessment.

Neurological review has been requested and no cause is established; the nurse has recorded the hearing difficulty and the disputed awareness episodes separately rather than assuming that one explains the other.
At today's review BP 174/102 mmHg was followed after rest by BP 158/92 mmHg, and he says he missed a blood-pressure tablet that morning.
He denies having lost consciousness or needing another person to treat the episode, although a supervisor says a colleague took over the loading paperwork because he seemed confused.

The driver reports diabetes managed with tablets, but an older specialist letter describes diet and exercise alone and the current medication box is not available for verification; he says the tablets were changed last month and has not used insulin to his knowledge.
